newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France plans global cargo alliances.
newsitem.headline: Air France plans global cargo alliances.

text.p: Air France Cargo said it will build up a global network of airline alliances to target fast-growing intercontinental markets.
Francois Bachelet, executive vice president and chief operating officer, said such alliances would allow it to offer freight forwarders daily capacity to the leading world markets.
"We must build alliances because we will never get the fifth freedom rights that would allow us to fly to the main markets of the world with our own means," he told Reuters in an interview.
"We can add more destinations than we serve with our own (traffic) rights by pre-forwarding to the partner's platform," he said.
"If there is a market which is not being serviced now because France has no rights to operate, we can sell through this partnership," he added.
Speaking after a Frankfurt reception, Bachelet, who took over as cargo chief in January, stressed that Air France had not yet selected its airline partners.
"But there will be several, in south-eastern Asia, China, northern America," he said.
Air France already cooperates with several airlines including Singapore Airlines, Japan Airlines and Aerolineas Argentinas.
Bachelet stressed that such a global network was vital if Air France was to be the chosen partner of the major freight forwarders.
"Then we can go to Schenker, Panalpina or Kuehne and say whatever your destination we can offer you a daily service."
Bachelet said the cargo partnerships and alliances would be a mix of fixed allotments or space sharing joint ventures or back-to-back operations.
But Air France did not plan single hubs in Asia or the Americas since it did not want to be over-dependent on a single partner airline, he stressed.
"Once we are daily to all these points either directly or indirectly with partners then the time will be ready to offer these partners more, a capital alliance perhaps," Bachelet noted.
